description: SOLO COMPOSER is a solo-led team participating in the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge. We are developing BUILDSCAPES: Apollo to Artemis, an interactive 3D Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer. The project combines space exploration, educational gameplay, NASA scientific resources and habitat simulations to make space science engaging and accessible to young learners. Our goal is to turn complex space concepts into an interactive learning experience.
summary:
**Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer** is an interactive 3D educational experience designed to introduce young learners to the challenges of human space exploration. Players take on the role of astronauts, undertaking simulated missions on the Moon and Mars, exploring environments, completing objectives, and managing essential resources such as water, oxygen, food, and power.

The project combines immersive first-person exploration, mission progression, habitat management, educational quizzes, and NOVA, an in-game mission guide character, to make space science engaging and accessible. Its missions are inspired by the lunar South Pole and Jezero Crater, helping learners understand the scientific and operational challenges of exploring other worlds.

By combining interactive gameplay with educational content and links to real scientific resources, the project aims to inspire curiosity, develop critical thinking, and encourage an interest in STEM among young learners.
details:
Source Code Repository:
https://github.com/thomasjoseph18/Junior-Astronaut-Mission-Trainer

Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer is a browser-based educational 3D game developed to introduce children to the challenges of human space exploration through interactive missions on the Moon and Mars.

Players explore simulated extraterrestrial environments, complete mission objectives, operate rovers, manage habitat resources, and make decisions involving water, food, oxygen, power, and radiation protection. The experience includes first-person exploration, mission progression, a journal, achievements, educational question-and-answer activities, multiple-choice quizzes, mission debriefs, and NOVA, an in-game mission guide character.

The lunar mission is inspired by the lunar South Pole and Shackleton Rim, while the Mars mission is inspired by Jezero Crater. These locations provide educational context for understanding planetary exploration. The project also provides links to scientific learning resources from NASA and Caltech.

The terrain is procedurally generated rather than rendered from downloaded NASA elevation datasets. NASA scientific resources are used as references and educational material, not as direct terrain inputs.

The project was developed using web technologies, including TypeScript, React, and 3D graphics technology. It combines interactive simulation, visual storytelling, and educational gameplay to make complex space exploration concepts easier for young learners to understand.

Its intended impact is to promote curiosity, scientific thinking, problem-solving, and interest in STEM through an accessible and engaging space exploration experience.
